correctness.rationale: The assigned n>=4 graph K_2 square K_n has exactly the open-neighborhood facet sets (A\{a_i}) U {b_i} and (B\{b_i}) U {a_i}. Each side is a collection of private-apex facet cones collapsing onto an (n-2)-sphere boundary; their intersection is the connected n-crown graph, with 2n vertices, n(n-1) edges and cycle rank n^2-3n+1. For n>=4 both sphere pieces are simply connected, so graph-to-piece maps are null and the cofibration homotopy pushout gives exactly two S^{n-2} and n^2-3n+1 copies of S2; at n=4 the combined rank is 7. For n>=5 integral Mayer–Vietoris identifies H2 with zero-diagonal, zero-row/column sum crown-cycle matrices, and top H_{n-2} with the two signed boundary spheres. The two negative signs from layer reversal of oriented crown edges and the ordered MV exchange cancel, giving transpose on H2. Euler-Lefschetz yields f^2-3f+1 and 2t-1, and the top traces are 2 sign and 0. Rational invariants under S_n vanish, hence so do the full finite-group quotient reduced rational homology groups. Independently reconstructed adjacency-derived simplices and GF(2) boundary ranks at n=4,5,6 yield precisely {2:7}, {2:11,3:2}, {2:19,4:2}; all 240+1440 signed simplex Lefschetz checks at n=5,6 agree. These finite checks corroborate but do not prove the all-integer statement, which follows from the complete homotopy and integral MV arguments.
